loop_primitives.evidence_quote: explored the interleaving of Chain-of-Thought reasoning (Wei et al., 2022b) — a method where a logical sequence of thoughts is generated — with document retrieval, repeatedly applying this process until the reasoning chain generates the answer
loop_primitives.note: Classifier routes to one of three fixed pipelines (no/one/multi retrieval); multi-step one is a ReAct-like retrieve-reason loop.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: our classifier can be formulated as follows: o = Classifier(q), where Classifier is a smaller Language Model that is trained to classify one of three different complexity levels
planning_granularity.note: Strategy selection is classification, not planning; no plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: this selection process is operationalized with a classifier, which is a smaller LM trained to predict the complexity level of incoming queries
multi_agent_topology.note: No agents or delegation described; a classifier routes each query to one of three retrieval strategies (ircot_qa multi-step, oner_qa single-step, nor_qa no retrieval), each run by one LLM. Coded single; the classifier-then-strategy flow is closer to routing than to a pipeline of specialised agents. Commit hash and line numbers are not in the evidence, so the locator is the README section only.

rollback.evidence_quote: Adaptive-RAG is designed to dynamically adjust its query handling strategies

termination_condition.evidence_quote: repeatedly applying this process until the reasoning chain generates the answer
termination_condition.note: IRCoT loop ends when the generation contains the answer, with a max-step cap in the jsonnet configs.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: we propose a novel adaptive QA framework that can dynamically select the most suitable strategy for (retrieval-augmented) LLMs from the simplest to the most sophisticated ones based on the query complexity.
cost_controls.note: Routing is by query complexity, choosing between retrieval strategies (not between models) to avoid 'unnecessary computational overhead'. This is the closest value to model_routing, so it is a mismatch; see ambiguity F2. No token budget or caching appears in the excerpts.

timeouts.evidence_quote: we measure the number of retrieval-and-generate steps and the average time for answering each query relative to the one-step approach
timeouts.note: Time is measured, not enforced; no timeout setting found in the shown evidence.
